steps_raw.instruction: 1 Pre-fetching culture solution: Take 6 ml of the culture solution in a centrifuge tube (operated in a clean bench).

2 Instant Dissolving: The cryotube containing the cells to be resuscitated was taken out from the liquid nitrogen tank and quickly dissolved in a 37-degree water bath for 1 min. The melted cell fluid was poured into a centrifuge tube containing 6 ml of the culture solution (operated in a clean bench).
3 Centrifugation: Centrifuge the tube into a centrifuge and centrifuge at 2000 r/min for 5 min. Discard the supernatant.
4 Resuspend: The cells are flicked by hand, and the tight cell become loose. The cell pieces are resuspended by 10 ml of the culture solution.
5 Pack culture: The cell-containing medium was dispensed into 2 small flasks in equal amounts of 5 ml per vial.
6 Observation and culture: The number of cell states was observed under a microscope, and cultured in an incubator.
1 Discard the old medium first. Wash 1 time with 1 ml PBS and discard the PBS.
2 Add 1 ml of trypsin-EDTA digest, shake it evenly, and put it in the incubator for 1 min. The cells were rounded under an inverted microscope. Quickly place the cell culture flask in a clean bench.

3 Add the culture solution to stop the digestion, gently puff the cells from the wall of the culture flask with a 3 ml culture solution, centrifuge at 2000 r/min for 5 min at low speed, and discard the supernatant.
4 The cell-containing medium was dispensed into 2 small flasks.
Cell cryopreservation

1 Remove the cells to be frozen from the incubator into a clean bench, shake the flask from side to side, and pour the waste liquid containing dead cells into the waste tank from the side. Wash twice with 3 ml PBS and discard the waste.

2 trypsin digestion: 1ml trypsin digestion for 2-3min, the bottle mouth is tight, placed under the inverted microscope to observe the cells. Over time, the original adherent cells gradually become rounded, causing the cells to detach from the bottle wall.

3 Termination of digestion: 4 ml of culture solution is used to terminate digestion, and the pipette draws the culture solution to blow the cells on the bottle wall to make it a uniformly dispersed cell suspension.
4 Centrifugation: The cell-containing culture solution was transferred to a centrifuge tube by a pipette at 2000 r/min for 5 min.

5 Cryopreservation: According to the number of cells to be frozen, configure a cryopreservation solution containing 10% DMSO in the culture solution, and use this cryopreservation solution to resuspend the blow , moved into each cryotube in a 1ml format.

6 Cooling: Place the cryotube in a programmed cooling box - 80 degrees overnight, and place it in a liquid nitrogen tank the next day. Record the cell name, operation time, location and operator's name.
Cardiomyocyte and cardiac fibroblast culture
Five culture dishes with an area of ​​10 cm2 were taken, the first two were added with 75% alcohol and autoclaved PBS, and the remaining three were added to the complete culture.

The SD rats were sterilized in a petri dish containing alcohol, and the hearts were placed in a petri dish containing PBS by using a scissors which had been autoclaved and traversing the heart at the chest of the rats.

The residual blood of the heart was squeezed out with a straight sputum and a curved sputum. The cleaned heart was placed in a petri dish containing the complete culture solution, and the residual blood of the heart was again squeezed out three times.

The heart tissue is cut into small pieces with scissors, placed in a centrifuge tube, and the heart fragments are deposited, and the supernatant is discarded. The culture solution was added to a 50 ml centrifuge tube and placed on an ice basin.

Trypsin was added to the tissue, immersed in the tissue, and the tissue was digested for about 40 s. After standing for a few minutes, the supernatant was aspirated and added to a 50 ml centrifuge tube in an ice basin. The above steps were repeated until the heart of the suckling mouse was completely digested.

The culture medium containing the cells was filtered on a 50 ml centrifuge tube covered with a 200 mesh filter cloth, and the filtered cells and the culture solution were dispensed into a 15 ml centrifuge tube. Centrifuge at room temperature for 5 min at 2000 r/min and discard the supernatant.
The cells were mixed with complete medium, transferred to a culture flask, and placed in an incubator for cultivation.

After standing for 1.5 to 2 hours, the fibroblasts are fully adhered to the wall, and the culture medium containing the cells in the upper layer is aspirated and placed in another culture flask (this is cardiomyocyte), and the cells are periodically changed according to the state of the cells.
1) The cells were plated in a six-well plate, and transfected without antibiotic culture solution for 24 hours.

2) Take two 2ml EP tubes and record them as A and B respectively. Add appropriate amount of Opti-MEM and the plasmid into A. B is added with appropriate amount of Opti-MEM and lipo-2000. Drop the liquid sink to the bottom of the tube and leave it at room temperature for 5 minutes. Note: This is the amount of one hole in a six-well plate.
3) The two EP tubes were mixed with liquid and placed at room temperature for 20 min.

4) Wash the plate twice with an empty culture solution, add the mixture to a six-well plate, and shake it in an 8-fold method. Incubate in a 37 ° C incubator containing 5% CO 2 for 24 h and change the solution 4-6 hours after transfection.
Lentivirus transfection

Pre-experiment of the target cell infection before infection, and determine the optimal amount of virus to be added in the case where the cells are not significantly damaged and the fluorescence expression is normal.

Depending on the type of cells and the time of analysis, the cells were inoculated to a 24-well plate the day before infection, so that the cell density at the time of infection on the second day was 60%-70%.
Dilute the virus stock solution in medium and add directly to the 24-well plate.
After 24 hours, replace it with serum-containing medium and culture the cells under normal conditions.

Digest the cells, place in a 1.5 ml EP tube, centrifuge, 2000 rpm, 5 min.

Add the resuspended cells to the flow tube, and take care to avoid light.
The fluorescence signal was measured with flow cytometry.

Taking materials: Digest the cells, collect them in a 1.5 m centrifuge tube, centrifuge at 2000 rpm for 5 min, and allow the cells to sink to the bottom of the conical centrifuge tube and discard the upper liquid.
Fixed: Add 2.5% glutaraldehyde at 4 ° C for 1-3 h to preserve the true structure of the sample surface;

Dehydration: Dehydrated with a series of gradient alcohols (30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 95% and 100%), each concentration of alcohol passed 2 times, the time should not be too long, 3-5 minutes each time is appropriate, Avoid shrinkage and even breakage of the cell surface.
Drying: Drying with acetonitrile followed by vacuum drying.
Spray gold coating: The sample can be observed under the microscope after being sprayed with carbon and sprayed with gold.

The cells were plated in a 96-well plate at a dose of 100 ul/well to ensure a cell content greater than 2000/well. The cells were cultured in an incubator (with PBS 200 ul/well around the wells to prevent evaporation of the culture medium).
When the cell density reached 90% confluence of the whole dish, 10 ul of CCK-8 solution was added to each well.
Incubate in a 96-well plate storage incubator for 1-2 h.
The absorbance per well was measured using a microplate reader (wavelength 450 nm).
Calculate the proliferation rate.
Preparation of lysate from cell culture
Place the cell culture dish on ice and wash the cells with ice-cold PBS.
Aspirate the PBS, then add ice-cold lysis buffer (1 mL per 107 cells/100 mm dish/150 cm2 flask; 0.5 mL per 5x106 cells/60 mm dish/75 cm2 flask).

Scrape adherent cells off the dish using a cold plastic cell scraper, then gently transfer the cell suspension into a pre-cooled microcentrifuge tube. Alternatively cells can be trypsinized and washed with PBS prior to resuspension in lysis buffer in a microcentrifuge tube.
Maintain constant agitation for 30 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge in a microcentrifuge at 4°C.The guideline is 15 min at 13500 rpm
Gently remove the tubes from the centrifuge and place on ice, aspirate the supernatant and place in a fresh tube kept on ice, and discard the pellet.
Measure protein concentration using cell lysis-compatible protein assay (BCA protein assay).
Boil each cell lysate in sample buffer at 100°C for 7 min.
​Loading and running the gel
Load equal amounts of protein into the wells of the SDS-PAGE gel, along with molecular weight marker. Load 60 μg of total protein from cell lysate.
Turn on power supply to 80V and run about 30 minutes. Change voltage to 120V when samples enter the stacking gel and form single narrow line.
Transferring the protein from the gel to the membrane
Activate PVDF with methanol for 1 min and rinse with transfer buffer before preparing the stack.

Arrange gel-membrane sandwich as described in manufacturer’s instruction. Place the transfer sandwich unit into buffer tank, fill with pre-cooled transfer buffer and attach the electrodes. Set the power supply to 200V and transfer for 80 minutes.
Block the membrane for 1 h at room temperature.
Incubate the membrane with appropriate dilutions of primary antibody in blocking buffer overnight incubation at 4°C.
Wash the membrane in three washes of TBST, 5 min each.
Incubate the membrane with the recommended dilution of conjugated secondary antibody in blocking buffer at room temperature for 1 h.
Wash the membrane in three washes of TBST, 5 min each.
Acquire image using darkroom development techniques for chemiluminescence.
